ai.description: *Micrixalus mallani* is a small, brown frog with a distinct light-colored snout tip. It features a slender body and long, thin limbs, with males exhibiting characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus mallani* is best distinguished from other dancing frogs by its unique, vivid orange-red throat patch, which contrasts sharply against its dark ventral side.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus mallani* inhabits the moist evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky, fast-flowing streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Male Mallan's dancing frogs perform rhythmic "foot-flagging" displays, extending and waving their hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus mallani* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in hidden stream-bed nests beneath gravel or stones.
ai.distributionRemarks: Micrixalus mallani is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, where it inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Micrixalus mallani* consists of a series of short, high-pitched chirps emitted by males while perched on rocks along fast-flowing forest streams.
